data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">What would be the implications of deleting an account from the technical perspective?</p>
<p dir="auto">It would be problematic, for example, if someone could immediately register a new account with the same username. Remote instances that may not be aware of the account's prior deletion would keep following the new, now impersonating account.</p>
<p dir="auto">So the username needs to stick around after deletion. Then every status by the user would be deleted, every deletion would need to be federated which might take a while (imagine deleting 40,000 statuses - you'd need to send the updated "deleted" status for every remote follower x 40,000).</p>
<p dir="auto">So this solution would be a soft delete then - as much information as possible is removed but basic structure and some pointers must be retained. So perhaps we could delete avatar, display name, bio, delete all statuses/media, unfollow everyone the account has been following, force all local users to unfollow it (cannot force remote accounts to unfollow though). Perhaps disable login on the account.</p>
<p dir="auto">That's quite a big task, isn't it</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button data-component="Button" type="button" aria-label="👍 7 reactions" role="switch" aria-checked="false" class="prc-Button-ButtonBase-9n-Xk reactionToggleButton__j2dnln" data-inactive="true" data-loading="false" data-size="small" data-variant="default" aria-describedby="_R_rage5gutkr85_ _R_rage5gutkr85H2_"><span data-component="buttonContent" data-align="center" class="prc-Button-ButtonContent-Iohp5"><span data-component="leadingVisual" class="prc-Button-Visual-YNt2F prc-Button-LeadingVisual-UySKu prc-Button-VisualWrap-E4cnq">👍</span><span data-component="text" class="prc-Button-Label-FWkx3"><span class="sr-only" id="_R_rage5gutkr85_">React with 👍</span>7</span></span></button><span class="sr-only" id="_R_rage5gutkr85H2_">Reacted by <!-- -->Alexander Yakovlev, Spunkie, Stanislas, Mathieu Bridon, Philip James, M-D-M and alizeh</span></div><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button data-component="Button" type="button" aria-label="👎 17 reactions" role="switch" aria-checked="false" class="prc-Button-ButtonBase-9n-Xk reactionToggleButton__j2dnln" data-inactive="true" data-loading="false" data-size="small" data-variant="default" aria-describedby="_R_1bage5gutkr85_ _R_1bage5gutkr85H2_"><span data-component="buttonContent" data-align="center" class="prc-Button-ButtonContent-Iohp5"><span data-component="leadingVisual" class="prc-Button-Visual-YNt2F prc-Button-LeadingVisual-UySKu prc-Button-VisualWrap-E4cnq">👎</span><span data-component="text" class="prc-Button-Label-FWkx3"><span class="sr-only" id="_R_1bage5gutkr85_">React with 👎</span>17</span></span></button><span class="sr-only" id="_R_1bage5gutkr85H2_">Reacted by <!-- -->Adrienne L. data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">There should definitely be a way to delete your account, from a data privacy perspective. I think it may even be a legal requirement in some countries to be able to leave a service.</p>
<p dir="auto">Most commercial services (Facebook, Twitter) seem to offer the option to deactivate your account, which hides all your content and gives you the option to one day return. Some then let you go further and remove your data from the platform permanently if you wish.</p>
<p dir="auto">For my part I opened an account on one instance before realising it was very localised to a country whose language I don't speak, then found there was no way to export to a different instance. I had to open a second account on the new instance, only to then find there is no way to delete my old account - which people can still find and follow. Very confusing.</p>
